metadata.title: CancerCompass — Comprehensive Cancer Knowledge Base
metadata.description: A curated, A-Z reference guide for cancer types, treatments, costs, and support resources. Compiled for patients, caregivers, and families.
metadata.disclaimer: This resource is for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. Always consult a qualified healthcare professional for diagnosis and treatment decisions.

india.title: India — Cancer Resources
india.overview: India accounts for approximately 1.4 million new cancer cases annually (ICMR 2024). Oral, breast, cervical, and lung cancers are among the most prevalent. Government schemes like Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY cover up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for cancer treatment.

usa.overview: The US has the world's most advanced cancer research infrastructure. Approximately 2 million new cancer diagnoses are expected in 2025. Medicare, Medicaid, and ACA marketplaces cover most cancer treatments.

items.name: Surgery
items.description: Physical removal of tumour and surrounding tissue. The oldest and most direct form of cancer treatment.
items.usedFor: Solid tumours — breast, colon, lung, prostate, gynaecological cancers

items.name: Chemotherapy
items.description: Use of cytotoxic drugs to kill rapidly dividing cancer cells. Can be curative, adjuvant, or palliative.
items.usedFor: Wide range — leukaemias, lymphomas, solid tumours

items.name: Radiation Therapy
items.description: Use of high-energy radiation (X-rays, protons, gamma rays) to destroy cancer cells.
items.usedFor: Breast, lung, prostate, head & neck, brain cancers

items.name: Immunotherapy
items.description: Treatments that harness the immune system to fight cancer. Includes checkpoint inhibitors, CAR-T, and cancer vaccines.
items.usedFor: Melanoma, lung, kidney, bladder, lymphoma, leukaemia, and many more

items.name: Targeted Therapy
items.description: Drugs that target specific molecular abnormalities in cancer cells (e.g., EGFR, HER2, BRAF, BCR-ABL mutations).
items.usedFor: Breast (HER2+), lung (EGFR/ALK), melanoma (BRAF), CML (BCR-ABL), and many others

items.name: Hormone Therapy
items.description: Reduces or blocks hormones that fuel certain cancers (oestrogen, testosterone). Also called endocrine therapy.

items.name: Stem Cell / Bone Marrow Transplant (SCT/BMT)
items.description: Replaces diseased bone marrow with healthy stem cells. Can be autologous (patient's own) or allogeneic (donor).

items.name: CAR-T Cell Therapy
items.description: Patient's T-cells are engineered to attack cancer. Breakthrough for certain blood cancers. Available in India since 2024.
items.usedFor: Relapsed/refractory B-cell ALL, large B-cell lymphoma, multiple myeloma

items.name: Precision / Personalised Medicine & NGS
items.description: Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) of tumour DNA to identify actionable mutations and match targeted treatments.
items.usedFor: Lung, breast, colorectal, ovarian, and many other cancers

items.name: Palliative & Supportive Care
items.description: Specialised care focused on quality of life, symptom relief, and emotional support — at any stage of illness.
items.usedFor: All cancer patients — not just end of life

items.name: Clinical Trials
items.description: Research studies testing new treatments. Often provide access to cutting-edge therapies at reduced/no cost.

cancerTypes.name: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL)
cancerTypes.description: A fast-growing cancer of the lymphoid cells in bone marrow and blood. The most common childhood cancer, but also affects adults.
cancerTypes.stages: Philadelphia chromosome positive (Ph+) or negative (Ph-) ALL are key molecular classifications.

prevalence.indianNote: Most common paediatric cancer in India

cancerTypes.indiaContext: CanKids KidsCan (Delhi) and St. Jude India provide support. Tata Memorial Centre, Mumbai is the premier treatment centre. ICMR-funded paediatric oncology protocols.

cancerTypes.name: Acute Myeloid Leukaemia (AML)
cancerTypes.description: A rapidly progressing cancer of the myeloid blood cells. More common in older adults.

cancerTypes.name: Adrenal Gland Cancer (Adrenocortical Carcinoma)
cancerTypes.description: A rare cancer arising from the outer cortex of the adrenal glands. Often diagnosed at an advanced stage.

cancerTypes.name: Anal Cancer
aliases: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Anus
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the anus or anal canal. Most commonly associated with HPV infection.

cancerTypes.name: Appendix Cancer
cancerTypes.description: A rare cancer of the appendix. Often found incidentally during appendectomy. PMP (mucus-producing) is a notable subtype.
treatments: CRS + HIPEC (Cytoreductive Surgery + Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy) for PMP

cancerTypes.name: Bladder Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer arising from the lining of the bladder (urothelium). More common in men. Strongly linked to smoking.
cancerTypes.stages: Non-muscle-invasive (NMIBC) vs. Muscle-invasive (MIBC) — critical clinical distinction.

cancerTypes.name: Bone Cancer (Primary)
cancerTypes.description: Primary bone cancers arise in bone tissue itself. Osteosarcoma is the most common primary bone cancer, predominantly in children and young adults.

subtypes.name: Osteosarcoma
subtypes.description: Most common; affects long bones in young people

subtypes.name: Ewing Sarcoma
subtypes.description: Second most common; affects children/young adults

subtypes.name: Chondrosarcoma
subtypes.description: Arises from cartilage; more common in adults

cancerTypes.name: Brain Tumour (Brain Cancer)
cancerTypes.description: Tumours originating in the brain (primary) or spreading to the brain from other sites (secondary/metastatic). Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumour.

subtypes.name: Medulloblastoma
subtypes.note: Most common malignant paediatric brain tumour

cancerTypes.name: Breast Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The most common cancer in women worldwide. Originates in breast ducts or lobules. Multiple molecular subtypes (HR+, HER2+, Triple Negative) guide treatment.

screening.recommendation: Annual from age 40–45 (US); 50 in UK NHS; earlier with risk factors

cancerTypes.indiaContext: Second most common cancer in Indian women after cervical cancer in rural areas; first in urban. Maina Foundation and Indian Cancer Society offer free screening. HPV not relevant here; genetic testing for BRCA1/2 available at TATA Memorial, Strand Life Sciences.

cancerTypes.name: Cervical Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the lower uterus (cervix), overwhelmingly caused by persistent HPV infection. Largely preventable through vaccination and screening.

prevention.screening: Pap smear every 3 years (21–65); HPV co-test every 5 years (30–65)

treatments: Surgery (LEEP, cone biopsy, hysterectomy, radical hysterectomy)
cancerTypes.indiaContext: India has the world's highest burden of cervical cancer — 1 in 3 global deaths. India launched Cervavac (indigenous HPV vaccine) in 2023. Ayushman Bharat now covers cervical screening.

cancerTypes.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia (CLL)
cancerTypes.description: The most common leukaemia in adults. A slow-growing cancer of B-lymphocytes. Often watch-and-wait at early stages.

cancerTypes.name: Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia (CML)
cancerTypes.description: Characterised by the Philadelphia chromosome (BCR-ABL fusion gene). Now largely manageable with targeted therapy.
treatments: Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (imatinib/Gleevec — first line; dasatinib, nilotinib, ponatinib for resistance/intolerance)

costs.india: Imatinib generic ~₹3,000–8,000/month; Novartis Gleevec access programme for low-income

cancerTypes.name: Colon Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the large intestine (colon). Often develops from polyps. Highly treatable when caught early. Rising incidence in younger adults worldwide.
cancerTypes.indiaContext: Colorectal cancer is rising among urban Indians. Tata Memorial Centre, Mumbai has India's largest colorectal oncology unit.

cancerTypes.name: Endometrial / Uterine Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The most common gynaecological cancer in developed countries. Arises from the lining of the uterus. Most cases present in postmenopausal women with vaginal bleeding.

cancerTypes.name: Oesophageal Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the food pipe. Two main types: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (mid-oesophagus, linked to tobacco/alcohol) and Adenocarcinoma (lower oesophagus, linked to GORD/Barrett's).
cancerTypes.indiaContext: High incidence in the oesophageal cancer belt (Assam, Jharkhand). SCC predominates in India due to tobacco-pan use.

cancerTypes.name: Gallbladder Cancer
cancerTypes.description: A rare but aggressive cancer. Often diagnosed incidentally after cholecystectomy. High incidence in northern India (Ganges belt, Gangetic plains).
cancerTypes.indiaContext: India has one of the highest global rates of gallbladder cancer. Particularly prevalent in women in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Assam.

cancerTypes.name: Gastric Cancer (Stomach Cancer)
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the stomach lining. Rates declining globally due to H. pylori eradication and dietary changes, but remains common in East Asia and parts of South America.

cancerTypes.name: Head and Neck Cancer
aliases: Squamous Cell Carcinoma Head and Neck
cancerTypes.description: A group of cancers arising in the oral cavity, throat, larynx, salivary glands, nasal cavity, and paranasal sinuses. Tobacco and betel nut chewing are major risk factors in India.
treatments: Pembrolizumab (1st line for recurrent/metastatic PD-L1+, KEYNOTE-689 data 2025)

resources.name: Support for People with Oral and Head/Neck Cancer (SPOHNC)

cancerTypes.indiaContext: Head and neck cancers are the most common cancer group in Indian men due to tobacco and betel quid use. India has 30% of global oral cancer burden. National Tobacco Control Programme (NTCP) is active.

cancerTypes.name: Hodgkin Lymphoma
cancerTypes.description: A cancer of B-lymphocytes characterised by Reed-Sternberg cells. Highly curable with modern therapy. Bimodal age distribution (young adults and >55).
symptoms: B symptoms: fever, night sweats, weight loss

cancerTypes.name: Kidney Cancer (Renal Cell Carcinoma)
cancerTypes.description: Arises in the lining of the renal tubules. Clear cell RCC is the most common subtype. Strongly linked to smoking and obesity.
symptoms: Classic triad rare. Often found incidentally on imaging

cancerTypes.name: Laryngeal Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the voice box. Strongly linked to tobacco and alcohol. Hoarseness is an early and important warning sign.

cancerTypes.name: Liver Cancer (Hepatocellular Carcinoma)
cancerTypes.description: The most common primary liver cancer. Strongly associated with Hepatitis B and C, cirrhosis, and NAFLD. Often diagnosed at advanced stage.
cancerTypes.indiaContext: Hepatitis B-driven HCC is common in India. Tata Memorial Centre and ILBS Delhi are leading centres. Universal HBV vaccination is part of India's National Immunisation Programme.

cancerTypes.name: Lung Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide. Two main types: Non-Small Cell (85%) and Small Cell (15%). Smoking is the main cause, but 15–25% of cases occur in never-smokers (often EGFR/ALK driven).

subtypes.name: NSCLC — Adenocarcinoma
subtypes.note: Most common, often non-smokers; test for EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET, KRAS

subtypes.name: Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC)
subtypes.note: Aggressive; strongly linked to smoking; often widespread at diagnosis

screening.recommendation: Annual for ages 50–80 with >20 pack-year history (US USPSTF 2021)

treatments: EGFR inhibitors: osimertinib (1st/3rd gen), gefitinib, erlotinib
Ivonescimab (HARMONi-2 trial data 2025 — outperformed pembrolizumab for PD-L1+ NSCLC)

resources.name: IASLC (International Association for Study of Lung Cancer)

cancerTypes.indiaContext: Lung cancer is the most common cancer in Indian men. AIIMS Delhi has India's largest lung cancer molecular testing programme. NTCP (National Tobacco Control Programme) is the primary prevention initiative.

cancerTypes.name: Melanoma
cancerTypes.description: The most dangerous form of skin cancer, arising from melanocytes. Linked to UV exposure and sunburn, especially in fair-skinned populations. BRAF mutation present in ~50% of cases.
symptoms: Lesion that bleeds or doesn't heal
treatments: Surgery (wide local excision, sentinel node biopsy)

cancerTypes.name: Mesothelioma
cancerTypes.description: A rare but aggressive cancer of the mesothelium lining (pleura, peritoneum, pericardium). Almost exclusively caused by asbestos exposure.

cancerTypes.name: Multiple Myeloma
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. Characterised by M-protein in blood/urine. Not curable but highly manageable with modern therapy.

cancerTypes.name: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL)
cancerTypes.description: A diverse group of lymphoid cancers. Includes >60 subtypes — indolent (slow) and aggressive. DLBCL is the most common aggressive subtype; Follicular lymphoma is the most common indolent.

subtypes.name: Burkitt Lymphoma
subtypes.note: Most common paediatric lymphoma in sub-Saharan Africa

cancerTypes.name: Oral Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancers of the lips, tongue, gums, hard palate, buccal mucosa. India has among the highest oral cancer rates globally due to tobacco and betel nut (areca) use.
cancerTypes.indiaContext: India has ~200,000 new oral cancer cases per year — one of the world's highest. ICS and CPAA conduct regular oral cancer screening camps. WHO has designated India for targeted tobacco control interventions.

cancerTypes.name: Ovarian Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Often called the 'silent killer' because symptoms are vague and diagnosis typically comes at advanced stage. BRCA1/2 mutations significantly increase risk.

cancerTypes.name: Pancreatic Cancer
cancerTypes.description: One of the deadliest cancers due to late diagnosis and limited treatment options. 5-year survival only ~13%. Often diagnosed when metastatic.

cancerTypes.name: Prostate Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The most common cancer in men (excluding skin cancer). Ranges from very slow-growing (often managed with active surveillance) to aggressive metastatic forms.

screening.method: PSA blood test + digital rectal exam (DRE)
screening.recommendation: Shared decision-making at age 50–55 (USPSTF); earlier for high-risk groups

resources.name: ZERO — The End of Prostate Cancer

cancerTypes.name: Rectal Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the last 12 cm of the large intestine. Treatment differs from colon cancer. Pembrolizumab for MSI-H rectal cancer showed complete response in 100% of a landmark 2022 trial (nonoperative management).
treatments: Pembrolizumab (MSI-H/dMMR — complete response without surgery in select patients)

resources.name: ASCO Nonoperative Management Cercek et al 2022

cancerTypes.name: Sarcoma
cancerTypes.description: A rare, diverse group of cancers arising from connective tissues (muscle, fat, bone, cartilage, nerves). Over 70 subtypes.

cancerTypes.name: Skin Cancer (Non-Melanoma)
cancerTypes.description: The most common cancers overall. Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) is most frequent and rarely metastasises. Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) has higher metastatic potential.
treatments: Mohs micrographic surgery (gold standard for BCC/SCC)

cancerTypes.name: Testicular Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The most common cancer in men aged 15–35. Highly curable even at advanced stages. Regular self-examination is key.

subtypes.name: Seminoma
subtypes.note: Pure germ cell; most common; exquisitely radiosensitive

subtypes.name: Non-seminoma (NSGCT)
subtypes.note: Includes embryonal carcinoma, teratoma, choriocarcinoma, yolk sac

cancerTypes.name: Thyroid Cancer
cancerTypes.description: The most common endocrine cancer. Papillary type (80%) has excellent prognosis. Anaplastic type is extremely aggressive.

cancerTypes.name: Uterine/Endometrial Cancer
cancerTypes.note: See Endometrial Cancer entry under E for full details.

cancerTypes.name: Vaginal Cancer
cancerTypes.description: A rare cancer of the vagina. Most commonly squamous cell. Often related to HPV.

cancerTypes.name: Vulvar Cancer
cancerTypes.description: Cancer of the outer female genitalia. Often SCC. May present as non-healing sore.

cancerTypes.name: Waldenström Macroglobulinaemia (WM)
cancerTypes.description: A rare, slow-growing B-cell lymphoma producing IgM paraprotein. MYD88 mutation is present in >90% of cases.

cancerTypes.name: Wilms Tumour (Nephroblastoma)
cancerTypes.description: The most common kidney cancer in children, typically occurring at ages 3–4. Highly curable with modern therapy.
treatments: Chemotherapy (actinomycin D + vincristine, or with doxorubicin)

cancerTypes.name: Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)
cancerTypes.description: Metastatic cancer where the primary site cannot be identified despite thorough investigation. Represents 3–5% of all cancers.
cancerTypes.diagnosis: Molecular profiling (NGS) can identify likely primary site in ~70% of cases.
treatments: Molecular profiling to identify treatable target mutations
